Additional Information: Room temperature strength tested using WDW-100 electronic universal material testing machine, tensile strain rate set to 1 × 10^4/s. Samples polished with sandpaper from 600# to 3000#. Hardness determined using Kanagawa Corporation's Model HV-115 Vickers hardness tester.

The presence of secondary phases might obscure basic mechanical properties. Single-phase solid solution alloys with refractory metals had difficulty in processing due to brittleness at low homologous temperatures. Compressive mechanical properties were influenced by coarse grain structure and chemical gradients. Two studies on rolled and recrystallized single-phase high-entropy alloys investigated room-temperature hardness as a function of grain size and preliminary tensile tests.
High-entropy alloys, solid solution hardening, good ductility due to face-centered cubic crystal structure with a large number of slip systems
